argument_macro_structure.dominant_argument_form: Dialectical progression from critique of atheological presumption to a post-epistemic synthesis, using Hegelian confrontation as illustrative case.
argument_macro_structure.premise_explicitness: Moderate; many premises are implicit in the critique of Shalkowski and the Hegelian analysis.

argumentative_quality.dialectical_reasonableness: High; engages with opposing views (Shalkowski, atheism) and attempts to show internal inconsistencies.
argumentative_quality.logical_relevance: High; all sections contribute to the central thesis of moving beyond epistemology.
argumentative_quality.premise_acceptability: Moderate; relies on phenomenological and Hegelian frameworks that may not be universally accepted.

dialectical_engagement.objection_handling: Acknowledges potential objections (e.g., atheists could argue for instrumental superiority) and responds by shifting to ethical grounding.
objections_raised: The game analogy could be seen as arbitrary

method_and_evidence.evidence_type: Conceptual analysis, historical illustration, analogy, hypothetical scenarios.

philosophical_orientation.grounding: Phenomenological and Hegelian, with analytic critique.
philosophical_orientation.sentiment: Critical of epistemology as sole arbiter; advocates for post-epistemic dialogue.
philosophical_orientation.thematic_focus: Philosophy of religion, epistemology, dialogue, presumption.

structural_organization.structure_type: Sectioned essay with introduction, critique, questioning, Hegelian analysis, conclusion.

summary_of_core_decisions: The paper decides to critique atheological presumption by deconstructing its epistemic rules, then to question the game itself, using Hegel to show the ethical-contextual origin of epistemic attacks, ultimately proposing a post-epistemic approach.

thesis_commitment.conclusion_type: Normative proposal for a post-epistemic philosophy of religion.
thesis_commitment.hedging_density_in_final_paragraph: Low; the conclusion is assertive but open-ended.
